Member spaces: A MEMBER'S PRIVATE ASSISTANT ON A DEVICE SHARED WITH THEIR TEAM (decided by Danny 2026-11-25; not a group chat). THE SPEC of every layer; TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/member-space.ts; web, desktop/CLI, iOS and Android replay the case lists.

DECISIONS: the DEVICE OWNER opts a device in per team, a TEAM OWNER may only switch it off; turns run on the logins ALREADY ON THE DEVICE; on a team device the Assistant works only in the teams that opted that device in; picking a team device starts a NEW conversation, the earlier one stays readable to the member and its key is never handed to the device.

THE OPT-IN: `devices.assistant_team_ids` (uuid[], synced, always a subset of `shared_team_ids`; unsharing a team drops it here too). `devices.setAssistantTeam {deviceId, teamId, allowed}`: allowed true = the device's owner only, the team already shared, kind server, and the device's doctor item `doctorKey` reads `ok` (else PRECONDITION_FAILED with the item's detail); allowed false = the owner, or an owner of that team (`dropAssistantTeam {id, teamId}` on the row id). `optInCases`.

A SPACE is a devices row OF THE MEMBER (user_id = the member, device_id = `space-<uuid>`, kind `server`, label = the host's label) with `space_host_id` (the host's devices row, synced, FK cascade) and `space_team_id` (the team it was picked through). Because it is the member's own device, every existing rule (host, claim, brief, readers) reads it as theirs. At most one per member (`uniq_devices_space_user`). It runs ONLY the trees of the member's Assistant conversation bound to it: every other start, child pick, move, agent, app slot or trigger naming it is refused (`startCases`), it is never a default device, never shared, and no client lists it as a device (Devices page, composer, pickers): clients drop rows with `space_host_id` (`listed`).

PICKING: `memberSpaces.request {deviceId, teamId}` (the host's device_id), in one transaction under the host machine's share lock (`lockDeviceShares`): the caller and the host row's owner are members of teamId, teamId is in assistant_team_ids, the caller does not own the host row; ends a space they have elsewhere (THE END below); creates the row; detaches the running Assistant conversation (status ended, agent_id null, stays readable, exactly as the Assistant move kept the dropped ones) and points the Assistant at the space (`agents.device_id`), its account = null. The next message creates a fresh conversation root there. `agents.update {deviceId}` away from a space ends it (so does `devices.remove` on its row, which an older client may offer its member; every other device procedure answers NOT_FOUND for it, and nobody registers a device id with `deviceIdPrefix`); agents.update TO a space or to a foreign shared device is refused: only `request` does it. A fresh request when a space on that host exists is idempotent.

TEAMS: `spaceTeams(hostAssistantTeamIds, hostOwnerTeamIds, memberTeamIds)` = the opted-in teams both belong to NOW, in the member's order (`teamCases`). The Assistant conversation's tree reach (`treeScope`) while its device is a space = its personal team + (its scope today ∩ spaceTeams). Children and chats it starts run in those teams only, and NEVER on a machine of the member's own (shared or not): while speaking through a space the only devices are the space itself (its conversation's tree) and machines of OTHER accounts shared with the team of the start, so nothing the host can make the Assistant do executes on the member's machines. That holds for a root, a child, a move, a continuation, an app's editor root, a default device, and for messaging, answering, configuring, resuming or ending an existing session that runs on a machine of the member's (`deviceCases`). What remains into a session on the member's machine: nothing.

THE CREDENTIAL: `memberSpaces.provision {spaceId}` (the host's own account, for a space hosted by its row) answers a fresh API key once, of the MEMBER, metadata {kind: `space`, spaceId}; the earlier key of that space is deleted. parseApiKeyMetadata reads kind `space` (malformed spaceId = grants nothing). Live only while the space row exists. OFF /api/mcp it reaches exactly `procedures` (tRPC paths, everything else FORBIDDEN) and `shapes`, with the member's team set REPLACED by personal + spaceTeams and sessions / messages narrowed to the space's own trees (roots = the Assistant conversations on this space, and sessions whose device is the space); on /api/mcp it is refused (an agent key minted through it is used). A session-argument procedure additionally requires the session to RUN on the space (its own device, in a tree of the space); a root argument one of its trees; X-Exp-Session-Id likewise, and `mcpServers.resolveForLaunch` / `skills.resolveForLaunch` require it; a machine argument only the space's; `sessionKeys.publicKeys` answers its trees and the chats its Assistant started since the pick; `heartbeat` answers no voice settings. Its steer control ticket names its device, and the relay refuses its `online` for another. A refused procedure = FORBIDDEN, a refused shape (table names in `shapes`) = 403, a key whose space ended = 401; Better Auth's own endpoints (/api/auth) refuse it. Attachments: GET only, its teams' issue files and its own trees' message files. devices.register/heartbeat through it touch only its own row and never kind, sharing, icon, label or default. An agent key minted through it (`users.mintPersonalApiKey`) carries spaceId, is limited to the space's own sessions / personal team + spaceTeams evaluated per request, and dies with the space. Off /api/mcp it is refused; on it every request speaks for a session running on the space (its binding or X-Exp-Session-Id, else 403), and its tools reach the space's trees and the chats its Assistant started since the pick (never the earlier conversation or the member's other sessions), start only where `deviceCases` allows, and change no device, key, install, approval or the Assistant's device. ITS TOOLS are an ALLOWLIST (`tools`, rows `<noun>_<op>`; a new op is refused until it is listed): tracker data, files, pull requests, reads and its own sessions; NOTHING that later executes with the member's authority or stands outside the space: no agent, trigger, schedule, prompt, skill, MCP server, app, record, event, status, board, team, member, device or CI write, no suggestion card, no other agent or app spoken to (`sessions_send` agentId / appId), no apps broker (/api/mcp/apps = 403), and an assignment made through it wakes no agent of the member. A root started through it (`sessions.via_space`, server-only, and every root such a chat starts) keeps the device rule for life. mcpServers and skills resolve only for those teams. No space key mints a space key, lists devices of others, approves installs or changes settings.

THE INSTALL: the space's daemon registers an install of kind `installKind` on its space row, through its space key, signed with `registrationLabel` in place of `exp-install-v1` (same lines), so a space install never verifies as an ordinary one. It reads (treeReaders) ONLY the Assistant conversation trees whose root runs on its space; it is in no other tree's reader list, `pending` or public key answer. Approval is the approval kind `approvalKind` (byte `approvalKindByte`), never `approve`; it always asks (the existing-installs rule and a first install never cover it). The approver is an approved ordinary install of the member's account. `installs.trust` serves space installs and `space` approvals, its own account's only, to a client that asks (`spaces: true`; released builds decode approval kinds as a closed set) and to the space itself; `installs.list` names a space to its member alone; `installs.waiting` lists it as `newInstall` with kindOfInstall `space`. One live install per space: a fresh one revokes the earlier and asks again. install-trust.json `space` holds the vectors. Until the member's `space` approval verifies, NOBODY wraps for it and the SERVER itself refuses wraps, pending listing and key creation for it. A client pins it as class `space`: it wraps for it, keeps its wraps and accepts its vouch only for a root that is the member's own Assistant conversation (`pinCases`). THAT ANSWER IS STICKY PER ROOT (`rootMark`, `rootMarkCases`), kept in the pin store beside the pins (`rootMarks`: root id → `assistant` | `never` | `unseen`, absent = none): the synced rows are the server's word, so a root this install ever saw as anything else (no agent, another agent, another starter, a child) never counts again, nor does one whose key it recorded before it kept marks (`keyed` without a mark: a space's conversation is always newer than that build). It is judged at every key record (R1 keep, its own new key) and every ask; a key recorded while its row (or its agent's) is not synced yet = `unseen`, decided by the first row seen. The RESIDUAL: a lying server together with the host's owner can present a root this install never saw as the Assistant's (a chat made elsewhere, its row withheld until then) and have a member's install wrap that root's key for the space. It can never approve, claim a root, reset or decline. The first key of a chat its Assistant starts (a root, `started_by_agent_id`) is made by it for that chat's readers alone, without a wrap of its own and kept by nobody there. Until its own approval verified in the space it claims nothing: a queued conversation stays queued. Its code shows on the host with `exponential members`.

WAITING: a conversation on a space whose install is not approved reads `copy.waiting` on the Assistant page and its messages stay queued.

THE END (`endSpacesInTx`, one transaction, `endCases`): causes `unshared`, `optedOut`, `memberLeft`, `ownerLeft`, `deviceRemoved`, `picked` (another device), `installRemoved`, `accountDeleted`, `removed` (the device owner's or a team owner's Remove). A space ends when its spaceTeams is empty or its space_team_id stops being one of them. Its keys (space + agent keys carrying it) are deleted, its install revoked, wraps dropped and the trees due for rotation (#EXP-1951), running sessions of its trees end (the conversation root goes idle), what those trees wait on (`session_watches`) goes and every unread input a SESSION wrote there (the agent's own, a child's, a watched chat's) is spent unread, so nothing the machine planted runs later (a person's own unread messages stay), agents.device_id = `` (empty: the page asks for a device, never a fallback to another device). While it is empty messages are refused: every send to the Assistant or into its conversation's tree (agentId, sessionId, a child start, a card's answer or tap, a call, a share target) = PRECONDITION_FAILED with `copy.noDevice`, nothing stored (a dismiss still closes a card), and its triggers do not fire and are not caught up. What was queued or unread stays readable in the old conversation; picking an own device continues it, picking a team device starts clean. The row goes. The member gets ONE notification for every cause but `picked` and `accountDeleted`. What the machine already read cannot be taken back.

THE HOST RECONCILES: on start, each heartbeat and each nudge the host's daemon calls `memberSpaces.hosted {deviceId}` ({spaces: [{spaceId, deviceId, member name}]}) and starts / stops child daemons to match; a stopped space first saves unpushed work to refs/exp-wip, then its directory is deleted. No answer (offline) = nothing changes, no new space starts.

ISOLATION: one child daemon per space, data dir `<data>/members/<spaceId>` (0700), in its own user, mount and PID namespaces with no_new_privs: it sees the system read-only, its own directory read-write, a private /tmp and /proc; never the host daemon's data dir or the owner's home, another space, /run/user, /var/run (docker.sock, the session bus), or SSH agents. Environment is an allowlist. The device's logins reach it as access tokens only (no refresh tokens), renewed by the host; no profile directory, transcript or settings of the host is mounted. A machine that cannot do this reports doctor `doctorKey` != ok and cannot be opted in; a space is never started unisolated. Linux servers only.

UI ×4 (existing parts): Settings › Assistant › Runs on lists the member's own machines as before (`runsOnRows`), then per team with opted-in hosts of others a section headed by the TEAM NAME (`spaceSections`, `sectionCases`), rows as ever (offline muted, disabled unless bound); picking one opens the confirm dialog (`copy.pick*`). The bound space shows as its host's row. Device settings › Sharing: under each SHARED team's switch the row `copy.optIn` (disabled with the doctor detail when it cannot), turning on confirms (`copy.optIn*`); then `copy.members`, one row per member with a space here with `copy.remove`. Team owners see the same off switch on the team device they do not own. Needs you shows the install row of install-trust.json, its label the host's label.
